citations.review_text: This game is pretty alright. As a simulator, its pretty basic as of now. Improve your shop, expand your shop, upgrade inventory, etc. But what i find to be the most entertaining, and somewhat addictive, part, is the ripping open packs. Ripping open 30-40 packs and getting one card thats worth several hundred or even multiple thousands of dollars is an absolute dopamine/seratonin dump for sure. Looking forward to 1.0!

Jank in the right ways. Card pulling is perfectly addicting.

Gameplay loop is a little long as of right now, needing to go through very long cycles of saving cash for your next upgrade. 

Looking forward to the planned content, especially a playable version of the card game

This ugly-ass game has no right being so addictive, yet here we are. It's really fun and deeply satisfying. Opening boosters scratches my brain just right.

10/10, would spray nerds with air freshener again.

As someone who actually buys and sells TCGs in real life, TCG Card Shop Simulator is an absolute blast during downtime.
It scratches that exact itch of running a card shop — stocking shelves with booster packs, cracking packs yourself for the dopamine of pulls, setting prices, dealing with customers, and slowly expanding the store. The collection side feels rewarding, and the loop of ordering product, managing inventory, and watching the shop grow is super satisfying without being stressful.
Perfect game to jump into for 20–40 minutes when you’ve got some free time. Chill, addictive, and surprisingly true to the feeling of the hobby. Highly recommend if you’re into TCGs or just like cozy management sims.

I hate that I love this game. Most of these shop simulators are all pretty much the same game but for some reason this one just scratches an itch. It is of all the ones I've watched or played just so incredibly fun and addicting. You wouldn't think stocking shelves would be fun but for some reason this game it is. Then on top of that opening packs.... lets call it what it is. in real life opening card packs is simply gambling but legal for all ages. This takes away the gambling part (with real money at least) and lets you gamble with fake money.

10/10 best gambling simulator yet.
Great cozy game, get lost in opening TCG packs

It’s a surprisingly good experience overall. The game starts off fairly slow, with only a small shop and a limited amount of stock to sell, but it doesn’t take long before you start seeing steady progress. Every new day gives you another chance to restock, unlock new products, improve the layout, expand the shop, and bring in more customers.

There are also plenty of upgrades that either make running the store easier or simply let you make the place look more like your own. You can focus on selling products, setting up tables for customers to play at, buying and selling individual cards, opening packs for your own collection, or just trying to make the shop run as smoothly as possible.

The progression loop is very satisfying because you’re constantly putting money back into the business and watching it grow. Even after many hours, there’s usually something else to unlock, upgrade, reorganize, or collect. And that’s before you even start trying to complete the full card collection, which could easily add many more hours on its own.

It’s simple to get into, relaxing to play, and dangerously easy to lose track of time while opening [i]“just a few more packs.”[/i]

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players note tedious manual pricing, slow staff members, basic character animations, and a lack of music variety or online multiplayer.

claims.claim: The inventory system needs quality-of-life improvements, staff members move very slowly, and setting prices on individual cards manually is described as tedious.

citations.review_text: I've played plenty of retail simulators. This is easily one of the best ones. It's specific focus gives the game a lot more charm. The inventory system could use some QOL improvements, and the staff moves intolerably slow, but these are pretty minor problems with an otherwise excellent game. The late game loop gets a little stale. It's basically opening endless packs to find that one super valuable card. When you find it though... it's so sweet.

TCG Card Shop is definitely one of those addictively satisfying games. At some point it definitely becomes repetitive but you always get an endorphin rush when you find a rare card again.

PROs:
-you can play this one for a long time while it still feels like you're making continuous progress
-there is a big variety of card packs
-there is multiple ways of playing it, wether you want to max your collection fast of want to earn the most money for expansions or just wanna decorate.
-there is many ways of automating but not too much imo
-you can move around really fast, things dont feel too slow

CONs:
-it doesnt seem important to most players but I think there should be child customers since a lot of kids play TCG
-setting prices on cards manually is tedious af, we need a shortcut for that
-rearranging the shop can be difficult, we need a way to store things in an inventory or some and also sell furniture
-I feel like my shops rating often makes no sence. I understand when customers complain about stink but why do I get one less star when my products are cheap? need better explanations on reviews.

I think this game is great for completionists like myself nd I will keep playing. I'd really enjoy some additions to the gameplay though to make it less repetitive.

BUG: the tutorial icon with the mouse is inverted, so at the start I kept clicking the wrong one

claims.claim: Reviewers note a lack of music variety, stating that only a couple of songs play continuously during gameplay.

citations.review_text:
This game is super addicting and honestly is exactly the game any fan of TCG should get.

Pros:

Graphics: Typical of a sim game, they "just work". They look decent enough to get the point across, but they arent going to blow your mind away. The cards look awesome and all the different styles and versions of the cards available is also good to look at.

Gameplay: The game shines obviously here. You can literally customize the shop to your exact liking, down to the decor on the walls. Everything is set up really nice to easily customize the store as you grow and add more as the money comes in. Honestly this game is way too dam fun. The little small jokes that TCG players know (Like smelly players) is also here. The tracking with its own TCG market in-game and the grading with its own TCG grading system is really in depth and well done. You can even pull god packs!

Value/Fun: The game is just fun, it really brings the TCG life to the forefront and i really enjoy it. The value is definitely here.

Cons:

Lack of music: Little to no music options. I believe theres only two songs that play the entire time. Maybe a jukebox option of some kind to change it up in the store.

Animations: Character animations are extremely basic. Characters move in a robotic fashion. When they are playing cards in the shop its a little better, but otherwise you are watching robots walking around your store. 

Honestly this game is way too dam fun and I am surprised how in depth all of it actually is. You will get a true TCG shop experience with this game and hopefully they continue to add more to the experience for the player, which it seems from their roadmap that is halfway done, they will hopefully do. 

Thanks for reading.

great game, fun simulator, specially for early access. I would recommend that they enable something to change the music though..the music does get monotonous with the music big time... 
Also when negotiating prices, sometimes the customers just refuse without trying to bargain if you bid too low..those 2 things should be fixed.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that late-game optimization suffers, resulting in lower frame rates and lag once the shop expands with more products, cards, and displays.

citations.review_text:
The concept of a shop simulator is nothing groundbreaking, but this game made it interesting by tapping into a very specific niche: TCG cards. The basic mechanics of filling your shelves, managing your inventory and upgrading your shop are all fun for a while, but what truly kept me going was the balance of wanting to collect every card vs. selling those cards to make money. Add on top of that the gambling mechanic of opening packs of cards and now you can't stop playing.

This was a great concept, but it was unfortunately packaged into what seems like a fairly low-effort game made with generic unity assets that still hasn't left early access after 2 years. There are many aspects that eventually make the game uninteresting such as the progression scaling being quite bad in the end game, and the fact there are actually way too many cards and variations of cards to have any chance at collecting them all.

No shame on the developer, they had a great idea, they worked on this alone, they made it happen and it blew up. The bad generic assets even help elevate its meme status. It is not a bad game at its core, you should probably play it if you haven't, but it's not a good game either. I would actually love to see a higher quality "remake" of this, but this version of the game is not something I would ever go back to.

I did complete this 100% because I really wanted to see what it had to offer, but it was a pain to push through and I mostly left the game running by itself with little intervention for most of my playtime.

I'm recommending because it's worth a play, just don't expect too much.
it was good for about 50hrs. then it got laggy lategame

Very good game, super entertaining and a lot of hours can go into it without you even realizing it, but it is just too unoptimized to be playable when you get to a certain point. Once your shop advances a bit and you start placing more cards / displays / products the fps just fully sink. I’m talking super choppy, 20/30fps max even with no customers in the shop.

Played the Chibi version on Mobile before. I love the collecting cards part. Saw this here as a 3d first person pov. Its quite relaxing. Early game is where you need more planning on how you progress on the game. Late game is like an idle. The rng for higher card value is a bit challenging. Im not lucky so its hard to get those that I need for the achievements. Hahaha. 

I finished the game and achievements. And one thing that is a problem. The optimization needs work for late game. Its so laggy, and I saw some complains about it too. Its not just me. The way you move when there are so many npcs or cards or boxes is so slow. It is good early game but late game is really hard. 7.5/10

love this game, wouldn't recommend it to my friends to save them the headache of the horrible optimization. once this is fixed the game is golden, you can forget about the rest of the timetable until the game can run decently.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that NPC customers can spawn in future expansion areas and become trapped during events like tournaments.

citations.review_text: This has been a fun game. There has been a time or two where customers spawn in the location of future expansions. Which happened to me during a tournament and 3 of the people in it were trapped so it never got out of the first round.

4.8/5 stars

I found this game after playing another cards shop simulator game because everyone online was talking about it. The devs are still adding features and there is a roadmap on the main menu, but no timeline.

You can get cards graded, but it's hit or miss on the quality. I have tried several times to get better graded cards by re submitting them, but most of the time they stay the same. I know it can be tempting to sell cards, but you'll make a lot more money by not doing so. The tables will also hinder your profits so don't waste your money on them until you unlock the ability to host tournaments. The more expensive tables serve no purpose other then aesthetics. As for the entry fee, it auto fills the amount needed to break even. I found that I can make the entry fee a little under the prize value for the fourth through eighth runner ups.

There's people that don't know what a shower is in this game and you will need to spray them to fix it. You eventually unlock an automatic sprayer to help with this but a few will still get through unless you only allow them to enter at one door. And set up two of them. I use the mid tier one that takes two sprays and the only time a stinker gets through is when it's a tournament. If this was a toggle, it would be great because they add no depth or strategy to the game. If you play with mods, there's a few that fix this very issue.

Money can be a little bit of a pain in the beginning because you unlock stuff before you can afford the licence, much less the merchandise so be patient. Customer will still come in and look for it, but you will be fine. everything has a value that shifts as time goes on. I don't pay attention to it and have my staff adjust everything to be 10% above value and rounded. All of my reviews say how cheap everything is but when I did 15%, my sales plummeted.

Overall, this is a fun game and worth the money if you can find it on sale.
